review_notes: I read the whole file. I checked Mathlib for existing CompHausAddCommGrp limits and found none; the Profinite group files matched only on other names. I compared the file's finite-diagram / partial-section machinery with Mathlib's `Topology/Category/TopCat/Limits/Konig.lean` and found a close parallel. I did not find a Mathlib lemma that gives the eventual-range characterisation of limit projections for compact Hausdorff systems. The explicit limit cone and its `IsLimit` are new to this setting, and `limitConePtAux` is a reasonable subgroup construction, so I did not flag them. The finding is a medium-confidence judgement: Mathlib's `FiniteDiagramArrow` is private, so reuse would need an upstream change or a shared generalisation. I did not check whether the file has a reason to avoid depending on `TopCat` here. Nothing else in the file seemed to be a competing concept.

findings.excerpt:
private abbrev FiniteDiagramArrow (G : Finset J) :=
  Σ' (X Y : J) (_ : X ∈ G) (_ : Y ∈ G), X ⟶ Y
findings.problem: The file re-implements the finite-sub-diagram partial-section machinery that Mathlib already has in `TopCat.partialSections` (Konig.lean). Mathlib has the same `Σ'` arrow type `FiniteDiagramArrow`, the same defining condition `F.map f.2.2.2.2 (u f.1) = u f.2.1`, and the same directedness and closedness arguments. The directedness proof is copied almost line for line, with the same `ιA`/`ιB` and `Finset.image … ⊔ …`. Here it is duplicated again inside the file, once for `partialSectionsAt` and once for `partialLiftsAt`. The only differences are an added basepoint (`PointedFiniteDiagram`) and an added constraint `s j = x` or `η.app k (s k) = …`. So the file carries a competing, slightly specialised copy of an existing concept, and its lemmas cannot interoperate with Mathlib's `partialSections`.
findings.proposed_change: Make the basepoint-free `FiniteDiagramArrow` / `FiniteDiagram` and `partialSections` in Konig.lean reusable. That means exposing them (or a version generic over a family of compact Hausdorff spaces, not only `TopCat`) so that `directed` and `closed` apply to `F ⋙ forget₂ _ CompHaus ⋙ compHausToTop`. Then express `partialSectionsAt` / `partialLiftsAt` as `partialSections F H ∩ {s | extra constraint}`. The directedness of the intersections follows from `partialSections.directed` plus monotonicity, and closedness from `partialSections.closed` plus `IsClosed.inter`. At the very least, factor the shared `ιA`/`ιB` union construction into one local lemma used by both `partialSectionsAt_directed` and `partialLiftsAt_directed`, instead of two copies.
findings.benefit: This removes roughly 60 duplicated lines of delicate dependent-type proof. It keeps one canonical notion of 'partial section' in the library, so improvements to Mathlib's version (for example the `privateInPublic` workarounds) apply automatically. It also makes the compactness argument here read as an extension of Mathlib's Konig lemma, not as an unrelated construction.
